title: Joint Enhancement and Classification using Coupled Diffusion Models of Signals and Logits
claim: Sequential or one-sided denoising pipelines ignore cross-information; coupling signal and output denoisers lets them guide each other.
layout: 4 vertical pipelines side by side, bottom-to-top, curved double-arrow in last
description: Four vertical stacks of rounded boxes sit side by side, each with data flowing bottom to top. Column 1 is a Classifier f_phi feeding a Softmax, with the label y_cor on the logit arrow. Column 2 adds a blue-shaded Diffusion X box below the classifier, with x̂_0 passing into it. Column 3 puts a blue Diffusion Y box between the classifier and the Softmax, with ŷ_0 on the arrow to the Softmax. Column 4 has both Diffusion X and Diffusion Y in blue, with a curved double-headed arrow on the right linking them to show coupling. White boxes are existing components and lavender boxes are diffusion modules. The eye goes to the lavender boxes and the curved arrow in the last column. The crop appears to cut off the bottom, where the input arrows and the (a)–(d) labels would be.
caption: Comparison of noisy signal classification paradigms. $\vx_{cor}$, $\vy_{cor}$ denote the corrupted signal and logits; $\hat{\vx}_0$, $\hat{\vy}_0$ their denoised versions. (a) {Noisy}: direct classification. (b) {Enhanced}: independent signal enhancement followed by classification. (c) {CARD}: denoising logits, $\vy$, given fixed corrupted signal, $\vx_{cor}$. (d) {Proposed}: coupled denoising of both signal and logits.
abstract: Robust classification in noisy environments remains a fundamental challenge in machine learning. Standard approaches typically treat signal enhancement and classification as separate, sequential stages: first enhancing the signal and then applying a classifier. This approach fails to leverage the semantic information in the classifier's output during denoising. In this work, we propose a general, domain-agnostic framework that integrates two interacting diffusion models: one operating on the input signal and the other on the classifier's output logits, without requiring any retraining or fine-tuning of the classifier. This coupled formulation enables mutual guidance, where the enhancing signal refines the class estimation and, conversely, the evolving class logits guide the signal reconstruction towards discriminative regions of the manifold. We introduce three strategies to effectively model the joint distribution of the input and the logit. We evaluated our joint enhancement method for image classification and automatic speech recognition. The proposed framework surpasses traditional sequential enhancement baselines, delivering robust and flexible improvements in classification accuracy under diverse noise conditions.
